blog/en/iga-antibodies-gut-brain-connect.title: Guard the gut's IgA, guard the brain
panels: I only cared about my brain…
To grow the brain, is it enough to look after your head? The starting point may be the gut.
The gut-brain axis: gut and brain trade signals in real time through the vagus nerve and the immune system.
IgA antibodies are the gut lining's first line of defense, and they protect the brain in the meninges too.
Gut care carries through to serotonin, BDNF and neuroplasticity.

blog/en/thoughts-are-not-you-act-cogniti.title: You are not your thoughts
panels: Anxious thoughts grow stronger and multiply the more you try to suppress them.
When you fuse with a thought, the amygdala treats it as a real emergency.
Label your thoughts, name them and thank them, and watch the popcorn in your mind.
When the prefrontal cortex takes back control, the emotional stampede stops.

blog/en/one-word-rewires-the-brain-neuro.title: One word changes the brain
panels: The brain takes the things you mutter to yourself as "commands."
Hebb's rule: circuits repeated together strengthen together, and a speech habit becomes a road.
The production effect: spoken words are etched three ways, down to Broca's area and hearing.
Kind words lower the amygdala's alarm and draw a new map of the brain.

blog/en/brain-fog-ketones-carnivore-ment.title: Why do I get sleepy after eating?
panels: After a carb-heavy meal comes brain fog, as if a mist has settled in your head.
When blood sugar rises and falls, the brain wobbles too. Ketones, by contrast, are a steady fuel.
Getting enough salt on a carnivore diet also reduces sugar cravings.
Mental clarity as the head clears. Results vary, so watch your body's signals.

blog/en/brain-health-plasticity-exercise.title: The compound interest of brain health
panels: The brain records exactly how you've lived. That record doesn't form overnight.
It changes as you use it
Thanks to neuroplasticity and the reward circuit, small repetitions rewire the brain.
An exercise habit is a matter of design, not will. Start by tying your shoelaces.
Today's single step builds like compound interest and changes your brain's future.

blog/en/post-holiday-reset-carnivore-die.title: A post-holiday quick reset guide
panels: Pancakes, ribs, rice cakes. After the holiday the body is a tangle of fructose, carbs and fat.
Cut carbs and blood sugar steadies as the body starts burning fat for fuel.
Add warm salt tea and well-absorbed chelated magnesium to a carnivore diet.
Avoid poorly absorbed magnesium oxide, and keep going while watching your body's signals.

blog/en/face-and-neck-lymphatic-massage-.title: The brain's drain: arachnoid fenestrations
panels: The brain cleans itself, but the first gateway waste passes through was long a mystery.
A study in Cell: 4.5 µm arachnoid fenestrations are the brain's drains.
Small habits like face and neck lymphatic massage become everyday care that helps the flow.
With age, the drainage passages shrink by 50 to 60%. Habits that protect the flow matter.

blog/en/what-changed-when-i-started-obse.title: When I started observing my day
panels: Fifteen minutes on a delivery app, twenty on a shopping site. My day was just drifting by.
Neuroplasticity: brain circuits really do reorganize toward where you often pay attention.
Record and observe your day, and purposeless time starts showing up in numbers.
Just as observation settles the day, action shapes a future that isn't fixed yet.

blog/en/the-early-bird-the-first-30-minu.title: The first 30 minutes matter more than rising early
panels: Social media the moment I wake
Even if you rise at dawn, skimming notifications in bed starts the day in a haze.
Sleep inertia: right after waking the brain is most vulnerable, and the cortisol awakening response kicks in.
Instead of your phone, start with a glass of water and opening the window. Guard the first 30 minutes.
A morning routine sets the day's direction with a sense of control and dopamine.

blog/en/one-minute-high-intensity-exerci.title: Just one minute: intensity wakes the brain
panels: Put off exercise because you're busy, and body and brain gradually dull.
Short, intense exercise boosts BDNF release through lactate signaling.
Slip one-minute bursts of intense movement (VILPA) into your day a few times.
Neuroplasticity wakes up and the hippocampus's memory circuits grow stronger.

blog/en/break-bad-habits-reset-the-brain.title: Reset the reward circuit with sweat
panels: Phones, late-night snacks. What keeps repeating despite your vows isn't willpower; it's neural circuitry.
The reward circuit of the nucleus accumbens and ventral tegmental area remembers and repeats intense behavior.
Link running to the same trigger for a healthy reward: the runner's high.
Recording micro-successes makes the new circuit stronger.
